gaps.sentence: Every morning she ___ an hour in the garden before breakfast.
gaps.explanation: 'Every morning' marks a repeated routine, which takes the present simple: spends.

gaps.sentence: Don't phone between seven and eight — we ___ dinner then.
gaps.hint: in progress at a stated future time
gaps.explanation: Something in progress at a stated future time takes the future continuous: will be having.
Visible present evidence points to a future event: 'is going to fall'.

gaps.sentence: I ___ you were coming today — nobody told me!
gaps.hint: state verb forbids the past continuous
gaps.explanation: 'Know' is a state verb, so its past form is the past simple: didn't know.

gaps.sentence: By the time I woke up, my flatmates ___ to work.
gaps.hint: by the time plus past simple
gaps.explanation: 'By the time' plus a past action refers back to an earlier past action, so the past perfect is needed: had gone.

gaps.sentence: She ___ her keys yet again — this is becoming a real habit.
gaps.explanation: The present perfect links the recent loss to the present habit.

gaps.sentence: She ___ three novels since she retired.
gaps.explanation: 'Since she retired' (up to now) — present perfect.

gaps.sentence: The conference ___ on Monday and ends on Wednesday.
gaps.explanation: Fixed schedules are stated in the present simple: starts.
